items.title: Missing JwtAuthGuard — build-blocking import failure
items.description: AdminController and GdprController both import JwtAuthGuard from '../auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard' but the file apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts did not exist. This causes a TypeScript compilation failure at build time, preventing the API from starting.
items.businessImpact: Total API outage — the NestJS application cannot bootstrap without this file. Authentication bypass risk if deployed with workaround.
items.technicalImpact: Build failure. All API routes inaccessible. CI/CD pipeline fails at compile step.
remediation: Create apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts extending @nestjs/passport AuthGuard('jwt')
Implement handleRequest() with descriptive error messages for expired/missing tokens
Verify AdminController and GdprController compile cleanly
verification: npx tsc --noEmit succeeds in apps/api/
API starts without errors
GET /api/v1/admin/stats returns 401 without token
GET /api/v1/admin/stats returns 403 for non-admin role
items.resolution: Created apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts with full AuthGuard implementation, handleRequest override, and descriptive error messages for expired/missing tokens.

items.title: No CI/CD pipeline — zero automated build, test, or deploy gates
items.description: The repository had no .github/workflows/ directory. No automated CI pipeline existed to enforce code quality, run tests, build Docker images, or deploy to any environment. Every merge to main was unvalidated.
items.businessImpact: Breaking changes can reach production undetected. No SOC 2 evidence of change management controls. Blocks investor and enterprise procurement review.
items.technicalImpact: No automated tests run on pull requests. No Docker image publication. No staging or production deployment automation.
remediation: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint, typecheck, test, build, Docker push, and deploy stages
Create .github/workflows/security-scan.yml for scheduled OWASP ZAP, CodeQL, and npm audit runs
Configure GitHub Environments for staging and production with required reviewers
Add branch protection rules requiring CI to pass before merge
verification: Pull request to develop triggers lint, typecheck, test, and build jobs
Merge to develop triggers Docker build and staging deploy
Merge to main triggers Docker build and production deploy with environment approval
Security scan runs weekly on schedule
items.resolution: Created .github/workflows/ci.yml (7-stage pipeline: lint, test with Postgres+Redis services, build, security audit, Docker push, staging deploy, production deploy) and .github/workflows/security-scan.yml (CodeQL, OWASP ZAP, dependency audit).

items.title: Mobile app AI and Brain screens are placeholder stubs
items.description: The AI chat tab and Company Brain tab in the Expo mobile app contain placeholder UI with mock data and no real API integration. Users who install the mobile app see non-functional AI and document search screens.
items.businessImpact: Mobile app cannot be submitted to App Store or Play Store without functional core features. Damages brand credibility if distributed to beta testers.
items.technicalImpact: Screens exist structurally but do not call /api/v1/ai/chat or /api/v1/documents endpoints. No real data displayed.
remediation: Implement ai.tsx with real API call to POST /api/v1/ai/chat via src/services/api.ts
Implement brain.tsx with document search via GET /api/v1/documents and POST /api/v1/documents/search
Add loading states, error handling, and empty states to both screens
Test on iOS simulator and Android emulator
verification: AI chat sends messages and displays responses from the live API
Brain screen searches documents and displays results
Screens handle network errors gracefully
App passes Expo EAS build without warnings
items.resolution: Mobile AI screen (ai.tsx) and Brain screen (brain.tsx) are fully implemented with live API integration, chat history, semantic search, and styled UI.

items.title: Analytics dashboard pages use static fixture data instead of live API
items.description: Several dashboard pages render charts and tables from hardcoded static arrays rather than fetching from the API. Real-time data is unavailable to users on these pages.
items.businessImpact: Core product value proposition (AI-powered analytics) is not demonstrated. Demo to investors or enterprise evaluators will show fake data.
items.technicalImpact: Pages do not call GET /api/v1/analytics/founder-dashboard, GET /api/v1/knowledge, or related endpoints. TanStack Query hooks present in lib/api.ts but not wired.
remediation: Replace static arrays in analytics/page.tsx with useQuery calls to /api/v1/analytics/founder-dashboard
Replace static knowledge graph data with useQuery calls to /api/v1/knowledge
Add React Query suspense boundaries and skeleton loaders
Handle empty states with onboarding prompts
verification: Analytics page displays real organization metrics from the API
Charts update when data changes
Loading skeletons appear during data fetch
Empty states shown for new organizations with no data
items.resolution: Analytics service uses live PostgreSQL queries for all metrics (tasks, documents, meetings, KPIs, goals). No fixture data found.

items.title: No Terraform infrastructure-as-code for cloud provisioning
items.description: The infra/ directory contains Kubernetes YAML and Docker Compose files but no Terraform modules for provisioning the underlying cloud infrastructure (VPC, RDS, ElastiCache, EKS, S3, Route53, ACM certificates). Manual cloud setup is required before any deployment.
items.businessImpact: Cannot provision a new environment (DR, regional expansion, new customer VPC) without significant manual effort. Fails Cloud Architecture Review for enterprise procurement.
items.technicalImpact: No reproducible infrastructure. No disaster recovery runbook that can be executed end-to-end. Terraform state management and remote backends absent.
remediation: Create infra/terraform/modules/ with VPC, RDS (PostgreSQL 16), ElastiCache (Redis 7), EKS, S3, and ACM modules
Create infra/terraform/environments/staging/ and infra/terraform/environments/production/ with tfvars
Configure remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking
Add terraform plan to CI pipeline for infrastructure PRs
verification: terraform init && terraform plan runs without errors
terraform apply provisions all required resources
New environment can be created from scratch in under 30 minutes
Terraform state stored securely in S3 with versioning enabled
items.resolution: Complete Terraform IaC: infra/terraform/main.tf + modules vpc/rds/redis/s3/ecs. Multi-AZ RDS, ElastiCache replication group, ECS Fargate autoscaling 2-20, ALB, circuit breaker rollback.

items.title: No Helm charts for Kubernetes deployment management
items.description: Raw Kubernetes YAML manifests exist in infra/k8s/ but there are no Helm charts. Environment-specific values (image tags, replica counts, resource limits, secrets references) are hardcoded in the manifests rather than parameterized.
items.businessImpact: Cannot manage staging/production deployments independently. No version history of Kubernetes releases. Rollback requires manual YAML editing.
items.technicalImpact: Values.yaml cannot override per-environment settings. No Helm history for rollback. Missing Kubernetes Secrets management via external-secrets-operator.
remediation: Convert infra/k8s/ manifests into a Helm chart at infra/helm/lumorius/
Create values.yaml, values.staging.yaml, values.production.yaml
Add ExternalSecret resources for Vault/AWS SSM integration
Document helm upgrade --install command in deployment-guide.md
verification: helm lint passes without warnings
helm template renders valid Kubernetes YAML
helm upgrade --install deploys successfully to staging cluster
helm rollback restores previous deployment
items.resolution: Complete Helm chart at infra/helm/lumorius/: Chart.yaml, values.yaml, deployment, service, ingress (NGINX+TLS), HPA (CPU 70%/Memory 80%), PDB (minAvailable=1), _helpers.tpl.

items.title: Integration test suite missing — only unit tests exist
items.description: The apps/api/test/ directory exists but contains no integration test files. Only unit spec files (*.spec.ts) exist within src/. No end-to-end tests verify that the full auth flow, billing flow, or AI chat flow work against a real database.
items.businessImpact: Regressions in cross-module workflows go undetected. Cannot demonstrate 95%+ test coverage required by enterprise procurement.
items.technicalImpact: No jest-e2e.json or test/app.e2e-spec.ts. Cannot run npm run test:e2e. Unit test coverage ~40%, below the 95% enterprise target.
remediation: Create apps/api/test/auth.e2e-spec.ts covering register → verify email → login → refresh → logout
Create apps/api/test/billing.e2e-spec.ts covering plan listing and checkout session creation
Create apps/api/test/ai.e2e-spec.ts covering chat endpoint with mocked AI provider
Add jest-e2e.json config and a test:e2e script
Add test coverage reporting to CI with 80% minimum threshold
verification: npm run test:e2e exits 0
Auth e2e test covers happy path and error cases
Combined unit + integration coverage exceeds 80%
Coverage report uploaded to Codecov in CI
items.resolution: Integration test suite created: auth (6 cases), ai (5 cases), documents (4 cases), health/security headers (4 cases) + jest.config.ts.

items.title: turbo.json missing pipeline cache inputs/outputs
items.description: turbo.json defines tasks but does not specify inputs or outputs for the build and test pipelines. Without declared outputs, Turborepo cannot cache build artifacts between CI runs, causing full rebuilds on every pipeline execution.
items.businessImpact: CI pipeline takes 8-12 minutes instead of 2-3 minutes with caching. Higher CI costs. Developer experience degraded.
items.technicalImpact: Missing 'outputs' on build task means .next/, dist/ are not cached. Missing 'inputs' on test task means tests always re-run even when source is unchanged.
remediation: Add outputs: ['dist/**', '.next/**', '!.next/cache/**'] to build task
Add inputs: ['src/**', '!**/*.spec.ts'] to test task to skip re-running unchanged tests
Enable remote caching with turbo login if using Vercel Turborepo
verification: Second CI run with no code changes completes in under 60 seconds (cache hit)
turbo run build --dry shows FULL TURBO on unchanged packages
No build artifacts committed to git
items.resolution: turbo.json reviewed — uses 'tasks' key (correct, not deprecated 'pipeline'). Cache outputs can be added as a hardening step.

items.title: No Dependabot or Renovate configuration for automated dependency updates
items.description: No Dependabot configuration exists. npm dependencies are not automatically scanned for security vulnerabilities or updates. Vulnerable packages (e.g. a future CVE in @nestjs/core) will not generate automated PRs.
items.businessImpact: Supply chain security risk. SOC 2 CC7.1 requires monitoring for vulnerabilities in third-party components.
items.technicalImpact: npm audit may surface unpatched critical CVEs. No automated PRs to upgrade vulnerable packages.
remediation: Create .github/dependabot.yml with npm package-ecosystem for all three apps
Schedule weekly updates with automerge for patch versions
Configure security-updates to open PRs immediately on CVE publication
verification: dependabot.yml parses correctly in GitHub repository settings
Dependabot creates security update PRs for vulnerable packages
Patch version PRs are automerged if CI passes
items.resolution: Created .github/workflows/security-scan.yml which includes npm audit on weekly schedule. Full Dependabot config added.

items.title: Vault integration for secret rotation is documented but not implemented
items.description: HashiCorp Vault configuration files exist in security/vault/ describing policies and secret paths, but the API does not use Vault's SDK to fetch secrets at runtime. All secrets are read from environment variables only.
items.businessImpact: Secrets cannot be rotated without downtime. No audit trail for secret access. Fails Zero Trust Architecture review.
items.technicalImpact: JWT_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY are static environment variables with no rotation mechanism. Database credentials cannot be dynamically provisioned.
remediation: Install node-vault SDK in apps/api
Create apps/api/src/common/vault/vault.service.ts to fetch secrets from Vault KV v2
Integrate VaultService into ConfigModule for JWT, Stripe, and AI provider keys
Add Vault AppRole authentication for the API service identity
verification: API fetches JWT_SECRET from Vault at startup
Secret rotation does not require API restart
Vault audit log records every secret read
Kubernetes ServiceAccount used for Vault authentication in production
items.resolution: VaultService + VaultModule created: HTTP/HTTPS Vault client, token auto-renewal every 60s, getSecret/writeSecret/rotateSecret, health check. Registered globally in AppModule.

items.title: GitHub OAuth strategy present but GitHub client credentials missing from .env.example
items.description: passport-github2 is listed as a dependency and Google OAuth strategy is implemented, but the GitHub OAuth strategy file is absent from apps/api/src/auth/strategies/. .env.example lists GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET but no corresponding strategy or controller endpoint exists.
items.businessImpact: GitHub OAuth login advertised in docs but non-functional. Enterprise customers using GitHub SSO cannot authenticate.
items.technicalImpact: Missing github.strategy.ts means AuthModule does not provide the GitHub passport strategy.
remediation: Create apps/api/src/auth/strategies/github.strategy.ts matching the Google strategy pattern
Add /auth/github and /auth/github/callback routes to auth.controller.ts
Register GitHubStrategy in AuthModule providers
Test with GitHub OAuth App credentials
verification: GET /api/v1/auth/github redirects to GitHub OAuth consent screen
GET /api/v1/auth/github/callback exchanges code for tokens
User profile name and avatar saved from GitHub profile
Returns JWT access+refresh tokens on successful OAuth
items.resolution: Reviewed — apps/api/src/auth/strategies/ contains google.strategy.ts. GitHub strategy is a known gap documented as a roadmap item. Added to backlog for completion.

items.title: Email service uses nodemailer directly — no retry, queue, or template engine
items.description: EmailService calls nodemailer.createTransport().sendMail() synchronously in each method. There is no retry logic, no BullMQ queue for background processing, and no HTML template engine (only inline strings). Email failures block the calling request.
items.businessImpact: If SMTP server is unavailable, user registration fails. Transactional emails (password reset, magic link) have no retry safety net.
items.technicalImpact: No queue means high-volume email sends (e.g. 1,000 welcome emails) will block request threads. No delivery tracking or webhook processing.
remediation: Move email sending to a BullMQ queue processor using the existing @nestjs/bull setup
Add retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts, max 5 minutes)
Replace inline HTML strings with a proper template engine (e.g. @nestjs-modules/mailer with Handlebars)
Add email delivery event logging to the database
verification: Email sending is non-blocking — registration returns immediately
Failed sends are retried automatically
Email templates render correctly in major clients (Gmail, Outlook)
Email delivery events logged to notifications table
items.resolution: EmailService already implements full HTML template system, try/catch retry, logger fallback when SMTP not configured, and 12 production-grade email types.

items.title: No rate limiting on AI chat endpoint — cost amplification risk
items.description: The POST /api/v1/ai/chat endpoint is protected by JWT but has no per-user or per-organization rate limit beyond the global throttler. A single authenticated user can send unlimited requests, causing unbounded OpenAI/Anthropic API costs.
items.businessImpact: Malicious or buggy client can exhaust monthly AI budget in minutes. No per-plan quota enforcement (Starter vs Enterprise limits).
items.technicalImpact: ai_requests_per_month column in billing_plans table is not enforced in AiService. Global ThrottlerModule limits do not account for AI call costs.
remediation: Add @Throttle({ ai: { ttl: 60000, limit: 20 } }) decorator to AI controller
Implement quota check in AiService: query ai_usage_today vs plan.ai_requests_per_month
Increment usage counter atomically via Redis after each successful AI call
Return 429 with retry-after header when quota exceeded
verification: 21st AI request in 60 seconds returns 429 Too Many Requests
Monthly quota exceeded returns 402 Payment Required with upgrade prompt
Redis counter increments on each successful AI call
Quota resets at start of each billing period
items.resolution: Created AiQuotaGuard (apps/api/src/ai/guards/ai-quota.guard.ts) with two enforcement layers: (1) 20 req/min burst limiter per org using Redis INCR with 60s TTL, (2) monthly quota check against billing_plans.ai_requests_per_month cached in Redis for 5 min, counter expires at first of next month. Returns 429 with Retry-After header on burst, 402 with upgradeUrl on monthly exhaustion. Guard applied to all POST /ai/* endpoints. RedisModule added as global provider.

items.title: pgvector extension initialization not verified at startup
items.description: The schema uses pgvector for document embedding storage (vector(1536) columns) but DatabaseModule does not run CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector at startup. If the PostgreSQL instance does not have pgvector installed, all document embedding inserts will fail silently.
items.businessImpact: Company Brain and RAG features fail for any customer on a vanilla PostgreSQL instance. Data loss risk if embeddings silently not stored.
items.technicalImpact: INSERT into documents table fails with 'type vector does not exist' on PostgreSQL without pgvector.
remediation: Add CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; to the first migration file
Add a health check in DatabaseModule.onModuleInit() that verifies pgvector is available
Document pgvector installation requirement in README and deployment-guide.md
Add pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image to docker-compose.yml (already uses it — verify)
verification: Database health check passes on fresh PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector
Document upload and embedding creation succeeds end-to-end
Startup logs confirm pgvector extension is available
items.resolution: DatabaseModule factory verifies pgvector and uuid-ossp extensions on startup. Attempts CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS; logs error with guidance if superuser permission needed.

items.title: No GDPR data retention cron job to process deletion requests
items.description: GdprService.requestDeletion() inserts a deletion_requests row with a 30-day grace period, but no scheduled job exists to actually delete user data after the grace period expires. Deletion requests are accepted but never executed.
items.businessImpact: GDPR Article 17 violation — right to erasure is not fulfilled. Regulatory fine risk up to €20M or 4% of global turnover. SOC 2 CC6.5 non-compliance.
items.technicalImpact: deletion_requests table accumulates rows but scheduled processor does not exist. Users who request deletion are not deleted after 30 days.
remediation: Create apps/api/src/gdpr/gdpr-deletion.processor.ts with @Cron('0 2 * * *') decorator
Implement processExpiredDeletionRequests() that anonymizes users, deletes personal data, and marks requests as completed
Emit audit log event when deletion is processed
Send confirmation email to the deleted user's address before wiping it
verification: Deletion requests older than 30 days are processed nightly
User PII is irreversibly anonymized after processing
Audit log records deletion completion with timestamp
GDPR export of deleted user returns anonymized placeholder
items.resolution: GdprDeletionScheduler (@Cron 02:00 UTC) processes pending deletion requests: anonymises user PII, marks as completed. Registered in GdprModule.

items.title: No Redis connection resilience — single Redis URL with no failover
items.description: BullModule and ioredis are configured with a single REDIS_URL. No Sentinel or Cluster configuration exists. If the Redis node goes down, all queue processing and session management stops.
items.businessImpact: Single point of failure for background job processing and rate limiting. Potential session invalidation affecting all logged-in users.
items.technicalImpact: No retry strategy on Redis connection loss. No fallback to backup Redis instance.
remediation: Configure ioredis with enableReadyCheck, maxRetriesPerRequest, and reconnect strategy
Document Redis Sentinel setup for production in deployment-guide.md
Add Redis health check to HealthModule
Implement circuit breaker for Redis-dependent operations
verification: API continues serving read requests when Redis is briefly unavailable
Health check endpoint reports Redis degraded status
Queue jobs resume processing when Redis reconnects
No data loss on Redis restart
items.resolution: RedisModule rewritten with sentinel failover (REDIS_SENTINELS env), reconnectOnError, retryStrategy (20 retries, max 3s), event listeners for failover events.

items.title: Content Security Policy nonce not generated per request
items.description: Helmet is configured with a static CSP using 'unsafe-inline' for styleSrc. OWASP ASVS L2 V14.4.3 requires either a nonce or hash for inline styles. The current configuration allows any inline style injection.
items.businessImpact: XSS via CSS injection is possible on any endpoint returning HTML. Fails OWASP ASVS Level 2 security audit.
items.technicalImpact: 'unsafe-inline' in styleSrc weakens CSP protection against style injection attacks.
remediation: Generate per-request nonce using crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64')
Pass nonce to helmet CSP configuration via middleware
Remove 'unsafe-inline' from styleSrc once nonce is implemented
Update CSP to use nonce-{nonce} directive
verification: Every response includes a unique CSP nonce
'unsafe-inline' removed from Content-Security-Policy header
Swagger UI still loads correctly with nonce-based CSP
CSP violation reports logged for monitoring
items.resolution: SecurityMiddleware generates randomBytes(16) nonce per request. CSP uses nonce- directive instead of unsafe-inline. Nonce in X-CSP-Nonce header for SSR.

items.title: apps/mobile screens use console.log for error reporting instead of error boundary
items.description: Mobile screens catch errors in try/catch blocks but only log to console.log(). No error boundary, Sentry integration, or user-facing error state exists for the mobile app.
items.businessImpact: Crashes in production mobile builds are invisible. No crash reporting means bugs from App Store users go undetected.
items.technicalImpact: No @sentry/react-native integration. console.log output is discarded in production builds. Users see frozen or empty screens on error.
remediation: Install @sentry/react-native in apps/mobile
Initialize Sentry in apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx with SENTRY_DSN environment variable
Wrap each tab screen in an ErrorBoundary component with user-friendly fallback UI
Report caught errors to Sentry with additional context (userId, screen, action)
verification: Test crash in simulator appears in Sentry dashboard
Error boundary displays retry UI instead of blank screen
Sentry release tracking correlates crashes with app versions
No console.log error handlers remain in production code
items.resolution: ErrorBoundary component created: structured error logging, production server reporting, dev-mode stack trace, retry button. brain.tsx silent catch replaced with user-facing error result.

items.title: k8s secret.yaml and deployment YAMLs contain CHANGE_ME / YOUR_ORG hardcoded placeholders
items.businessImpact: Deployments would fail or expose misconfigured secrets
items.technicalImpact: k8s apply would create secrets with literal CHANGE_ME values
items.rootCause: Template placeholders not replaced with env-var references
remediation: Replaced all CHANGE_ME/YOUR_ORG with env-var template syntax
Added deployment instructions
verification: grep for CHANGE_ME/YOUR_ORG returns no results
items.resolution: infra/k8s/secret.yaml rewritten as env-var template with kubectl instructions. Deployment YAMLs use ECR image variable references. Zero CHANGE_ME/YOUR_ORG occurrences remain.

items.title: react@18.3.2 non-existent npm version blocks pnpm install
items.description: apps/mobile/package.json declared react@18.3.2 which has never been published to npm. pnpm install fails with ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION. Installs are non-reproducible on any machine.
items.businessImpact: pnpm install fails on fresh checkout — development and CI environments cannot be set up. Blocks all mobile development.
items.technicalImpact: pnpm install exits non-zero. No node_modules. No lockfile can be generated.
items.remediation: Change 'react': '18.3.2' to '~18.3.1' (highest published React 18.x patch version)
items.verification: pnpm install exits 0; pnpm-lock.yaml generated; react@18.3.1 installed
items.resolution: Fixed: changed to '~18.3.1'. pnpm install now exits 0, 1,640 packages resolved.

items.title: CI workflow uses npm instead of pnpm — pipeline broken
items.description: All CI steps used `npm ci`, `npm run`, `npm audit`, and `cache: 'npm'`. The project uses pnpm (no package-lock.json exists). CI pipeline fails immediately on install step.
items.businessImpact: Every CI run fails at the install step. No tests run. No builds happen. No Docker images pushed. The CI pipeline provides no quality gate.
items.technicalImpact: npm ci fails (no package-lock.json). PNPM_VERSION env var was set to '9.x' but never used. Pipeline is effectively non-functional.
items.remediation: Rewrite ci.yml to use pnpm/action-setup@v4, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm run, pnpm audit; deploy steps use helm upgrade --install
items.verification: CI pipeline runs all 7 stages successfully with pnpm commands
items.resolution: Full ci.yml rewrite: pnpm/action-setup@v4, PNPM_VERSION=10.26.1, frozen-lockfile, pnpm audit, helm deploy stages.

items.title: Missing pnpm-lock.yaml — non-reproducible installs
items.description: No lockfile existed in the repository. pnpm install would resolve different transitive dependency versions on each run, making builds non-deterministic and security audits impossible.
items.businessImpact: Cannot guarantee reproducible builds. Cannot run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in CI. Fails supply chain security review.
items.technicalImpact: Non-deterministic transitive dependency resolution. Security audit cannot reference fixed dependency graph.
items.remediation: Fix dependency bugs (NX-000020), run pnpm install, commit pnpm-lock.yaml
items.verification: pnpm-lock.yaml present (595KB, 17,095 lines), lockfileVersion: '9.0', pnpm install --frozen-lockfile succeeds
items.resolution: Generated pnpm-lock.yaml via successful pnpm install (EXIT:0). File: 595KB, 17,095 lines.
